chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim and others narrated to us, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from al-Husayn ibn Zayd al-Hashimi, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:

Zaynab, the squint-eyed perfume seller, came to the wives of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his daughters, and she used to sell perfume to them. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered while she was with them, and said to her: 'When you visit us, our houses become fragrant.' She said: 'Your houses are more fragrant due to your scent, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'When you sell, be good and do not deceive, for that is more pious and preserves wealth better.' She said: 'I did not come with anything from my selling, but I came to ask you about the Greatness of Allah.' He said: 'Glory be to His Majesty, I will tell you about some of that.'

He said: Then he said: 'Verily, this earth, with what is in it and on it, in relation to what is beneath it, is like a ring in a vast desert. And these two (earth and what is below it), with what is in them and on them, in relation to what is beneath them, are like a ring in a vast desert. And the third, until he reached the seventh.'
"He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them."

And the seven heavens, and what is in them and on them, on the back of the rooster are like a ring in a vast desert. The rooster has two wings, one in the East and one in the West, and its feet are at the boundaries. And the seven, the rooster, and what is in them and on them, on the rock are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, and what is in them and on them, on the back of the fish are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, and the fish, in relation to the dark sea are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, the fish, and the dark sea, in relation to the air are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, the fish, the dark sea, and the air, in relation to the earth (dust) are like a ring in a vast desert.
"To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is in the earth and what is between them two and what is beneath the earth."

Then the report continued. And the seven, the rooster, the rock, the fish, the dark sea, the air, and the earth, with what is in them and on them, in relation to the sky are like a ring in a vast desert. And this (the lower level) and the lowest heaven, and what is in it and on it, in relation to what is above it are like a ring in a vast desert. And this and these two heavens, in relation to the third are like a ring in a vast desert. And this third, and what is in them and on them, in relation to the fourth are like a ring in a vast desert, until he reached the seventh. And these seven, and what is in them and on them, in relation to the sea that covers the people of the earth are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven and the covering sea, in relation to the mountains of hail are like a ring in a vast desert.
"And He sends down from the sky mountains (clouds) having within them hail."

And these seven, the covering sea, the mountains of hail, and the veils, in relation to the veils of light are like a ring in a vast desert. And they are seventy thousand veils, whose light blinds the eyes. And these seven, the covering sea, the mountains of hail, and the veils, in relation to the air in which hearts are bewildered are like a ring in a vast desert. And the seven, the covering sea, the mountains of hail, the veils, and the air, in relation to the Throne ( Kursi ) are like a ring in a vast desert.
"His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not, and He is the Most High, the Great."
And these seven, the covering sea, the mountains of hail, the veils, the air, and the Kursi, in relation to the Throne (Arsh) are like a ring in a vast desert.
"The Most Merciful rose over the Throne."
The angels carry it (the Throne) except by saying: 'There is no god but Allah, and there is no power and no strength except with Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the cosmological hierarchy of the universe according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in the hadith of Zaynab al-Attara?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* employs the metaphor of 'halqa fi falaq' (a ring in a vast desert) to illustrate the relative scale of cosmic layers, emphasizing Allah’s infinite majesty over finite creation. It systematically ascends from the earth through the seven heavens, the rooster (Dajjaj), the rock (Sadr al-Ard), the fish (Hut), the dark sea, air, veils of light, the Kursi, and finally the Arsh, grounding these cosmological concepts in Shia theological tradition. The hadith concludes by linking this cosmic structure to the angels' constant glorification, reinforcing the unity of creation under divine sovereignty.
